title: Apple Pie Stuffed French Toast
changes_from_base: Instead of slices soaked in a yolk-rich milk custard, cream cheese, apple butter and cinnamon are sandwiched between plain bread, dipped in a thin egg, flour and water batter and fried crisp.
summary: Crisp golden sandwiches hiding a warm pocket of spiced cream cheese and apple, finished with a drizzle of maple syrup.

ingredients.item: slices good white sandwich bread (about 280 g)

steps.title: Blend
steps.text: Beat together 113 g cream cheese, 3 tbsp apple butter, 1½ tbsp caster sugar and ¼ tsp cinnamon until creamy and well combined.

steps.title: Sandwich
steps.text: Spread the filling over 4 of the 8 bread slices, then close each with a second slice and press the edges together.

steps.title: Whisk
steps.text: In a shallow dish, whisk 1 egg with 240 ml cold water, 65 g plain flour and 1 tsp vanilla into a thin, smooth batter.

steps.title: Fry first batch
steps.text: Melt half of the 56 g butter in a large non-stick pan over medium heat, dip two sandwiches quickly on both sides, letting excess batter drip off, then fry until deeply golden, about 3 min per side.

steps.title: Fry second batch
steps.text: Melt the remaining butter in the pan and cook the last two sandwiches in the same way.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Slice each sandwich into triangles and bring to the table straight away with 60 ml maple syrup.

tips: Dip each sandwich only briefly in the thin batter; a quick dip gives a crisp coating without making the bread soggy.
Press the bread edges firmly together so the filling doesn't escape while frying.
Keep the pan at medium heat so the outside browns before the filling overheats.
safety: Frying safety: use a heavy, deep pot no more than half full of oil, with a clip-on thermometer, and dry the food before it goes in. Never leave hot oil unattended. If the oil catches fire, turn off the heat and cover the pot with a metal lid or use a fire extinguisher; never use water.
The filling stays very hot after frying; let the sandwiches sit for a minute off the heat before slicing.
storage: Best enjoyed straight away while crisp; if needed, keep covered in the fridge for up to a day and warm through in a pan before serving. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
